editorial:
Imagine you are a struggling writer who just wants to be famous. You find an old, unpublished book and decide to put your own name on it. That is exactly what Rory Jansen does, and it works perfectly. He becomes a superstar overnight, but the guilt starts to eat him alive. The movie feels like a slow burn that keeps you wondering if he will get caught. It is a story about greed, secrets, and how far some people will go just to be noticed by the world.

Bradley Cooper does a great job showing the stress of living a lie. The plot has some clever twists that keep you guessing about who actually wrote the book and why. While some parts feel a bit slow, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you like stories about secrets and redemption, you should check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you really love the cinematography, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: You find out that the book was actually written by an old man named Clay. Rory eventually meets him and confesses his crime. Clay forgives him, but the real lesson is about the three words: I love you. Rory learns that fame is nothing compared to family. He gives the credit back to the original author and finds peace with his conscience, finally choosing honesty over his own ego.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about secrets and moral dilemmas.
